pages.text: "Wow, bread!" Impatient Bobo rushed to the long window table. Teacher Bau placed one slice on each plate. "Noodles for lunch today," Teacher Bau said.
Bobo finished the bread in three bites, then returned with an empty plate. The next slice disappeared in no time too.
"One more slice, please!" Bobo offered the empty plate again. Gaga, who knew best, said, "You will not be able to eat lunch." Empty plates stacked before Bobo: one, two, three.
Ding went the bell, and lunch noodles arrived, steaming. But Bobo's tummy was so full that not a bite would fit. "Mmm... but I like noodles." Bobo put down the chopsticks.
Teacher Bau lined up three empty plates beside the noodle bowl. "Three slices are already in your tummy. No room for noodles." Bobo quietly looked at the plates.
Teacher Bau left one plate and removed two. "One plate—leave room for lunch!" Bobo repeated, "One plate—leave room for lunch!"
The next morning, bread plates appeared again. Bobo finished one slice and set the empty plate firmly on the table. Wanting more, Bobo kept both feet planted and waited.
Teacher Bau sat beside Bobo. "Your tummy will rumble again at lunchtime. Then it needs room for noodles." Bobo placed a hand on their belly and waited.
Ding, the lunch bell! Bobo's tummy rumbled. Pulling the hat brim forward, Bobo slurped up all the noodles. "One, one plate for snack! Two, set the plate down! Three, leave room for lunch!"
Teacher Bau stroked Bobo's back with a big palm. A little snack made lunch much tastier. "One plate—leave room for lunch!" Bobo held up the empty noodle bowl.
